name: Stat

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.code:
<Stat
  label="Revenue"
  value={8456.4}
  format={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' }}
  locale="en-US"
  change={0.12}
  description="since last month"
/>

examples.title: A Row of Stats
examples.code:
<>
  <Title as="h2" size="5" id="stat-kpis">
    This month
  </Title>
  <Stats aria-labelledby="stat-kpis" minCol={8} gap={4}>
    <Stat
      label="Revenue"
      value={8456.4}
      format={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' }}
      locale="en-US"
      change={0.12}
    />
    <Stat label="New customers" value={1234} locale="en-US" change={-0.019} />
    <Stat
      label="Churn"
      value={0.021}
      format={{ style: 'percent', maximumFractionDigits: 1 }}
      locale="en-US"
      change={0.004}
      changeColor="danger"
    />
  </Stats>
</>

examples.title: A Figure That Should Be Announced
Compound (dot-notation) usage
examples.code:
<Stats minCol={10} gap={4}>
  <Stat>
    <Stat.Label>
      Storage used{' '}
      <Popover
        ariaLabel="About storage used"
        trigger={
          <Button size="small" color="ghost" aria-label="About storage used">
            <Icon name="circle-info" />
          </Button>
        }
      >
        <Popover.Body>Photos, files and backups.</Popover.Body>
      </Popover>
    </Stat.Label>
    <Stat.Value display="flex" alignItems="center" gap="3">
      <RingProgress value={62} size="small" label="Storage used">
        62%
      </RingProgress>
      <NumberFormatter
        value={31}
        format={{ style: 'unit', unit: 'gigabyte' }}
        locale="en-US"
      />
    </Stat.Value>
    <Stat.Description>of 50 GB</Stat.Description>
  </Stat>
  <Stat>
    <Stat.Label>Median response time</Stat.Label>
    <Stat.Value>
      <NumberFormatter
        value={182}
        format={{ style: 'unit', unit: 'millisecond' }}
        locale="en-US"
      />
    </Stat.Value>
    <Stat.Change value={-0.08} color="success" locale="en-US" />
  </Stat>
</Stats>

accessibility:
- **HTML's own elements, and no roles:** a `<dl>` on its own, or a `<div>` in the row's `<dl>`,
  with a `<dt>` for the label and a `<dd>` each for the figure, the change and the note. Browsers
  expose them as a list, a term and its definitions, so a screen reader reads the label, then the
  figure, the change and the note, in that order.
- **The direction is in the text's sign:** the default format writes a change with its sign,
  "+12%" or "-1.9%", in the locale's form, so a screen reader hears it with no extra words to
  translate. The arrow is hidden
  from assistive tech, and the color repeats the direction rather than carry it.
- **Contrast:** the label and the note are in Bulma's `text-weak`, and a change in its color's
  `-on-scheme` variant, the one Bulma adjusts for text on the scheme's background. Each clears
  WCAG's 4.5:1 against Bulma's page background in light and dark mode.
- **Forced colors:** the text and the arrow take the system's text color, so the tone is gone and
  the sign and the arrow carry the direction. The loading `Skeleton` is drawn as a background,
  which forced colors removes, so there the figure's place is empty while it loads.
- **Loading:** `aria-busy` on the Stat while the `Skeleton` shows.
- **Not interactive and not live:** it has no tab stop and announces nothing when it changes; see
  [A Figure That Should Be Announced](https://bestax.io/docs/api/elements/stat#a-figure-that-should-be-announced).
- **Info tips:** a real button named "About" and the label, opening a `Popover`, as in the
  [compound example](https://bestax.io/docs/api/elements/stat#compound-dot-notation-usage), rather than a tip that opens on hover.
summary: The `Stat` component shows a figure with its name, and often a change and a note, such as a dashboard's revenue or an account's storage used. It's a label and its values in a description list: a `<dt>` for the label, and a `<dd>` each for the figure, the change and the note. On its own it renders its own `<dl>`; inside `Stats` it's a `<div>` in the row's. A number `value` is written by `NumberFormatter`, so it follows a `LocaleProvider`. A change is written with its sign ("+12%"), so the direction is in the text, beside a decorative arrow and a color.

parts.summary: The `Stat` component shows a figure with its name, and often a change and a note, such as a dashboard's revenue or an account's storage used. It's a label and its values in a description list: a `<dt>` for the label, and a `<dd>` each for the figure, the change and the note. On its own it renders its own `<dl>`; inside `Stats` it's a `<div>` in the row's. A number `value` is written by `NumberFormatter`, so it follows a `LocaleProvider`. A change is written with its sign ("+12%"), so the direction is in the text, beside a decorative arrow and a color.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes to apply.

props.name: label
props.description: What the figure is ("Revenue"), as a `Stat.Label` before the children. A Stat needs one, here or as a `Stat.Label` child: it's the figure's name for assistive tech, and a definition list's values belong to a term. A Stat with neither a `label` nor a `Stat.Label` child warns in development.

props.name: value
props.description: The figure, as a `Stat.Value` after the children. A number is written by `NumberFormatter` with `format` and `locale`; anything else, such as "N/A", renders as given, and `0` renders. `undefined`, `null`, a boolean and `''` leave it empty, and its `<dd>` still renders, one line of the figure tall, while the Stat has a label, so the label keeps its definition while the figure is missing. A `Stat.Value` child takes its place: with one, `value` and its `<dd>` are left out.

props.name: format
props.description: `Intl.NumberFormat` options for a number `value`, as NumberFormatter's `format`. A `value` that isn't a number ignores it.

props.name: locale
props.description: The locale for `value` and `change`, as NumberFormatter's `locale`. Unset, it's the `LocaleProvider`'s around it, and with neither, the runtime's own, so give one, here or through a `LocaleProvider`, on a page rendered on the server.

props.name: change
props.description: The change, as a `Stat.Change` after the value. With the default format it's a fraction (`0.12` for 12%); with your own `changeFormat`, it's in that format's terms. It's written with its sign, so the direction is in the text.

props.name: changeFormat
props.description: `Intl.NumberFormat` options for `change`. Yours replace the default, and `signDisplay: 'exceptZero'` is added unless you set a `signDisplay`. With `signDisplay: 'never'`, or `'negative'` on a rise, the text carries no direction: the arrow is hidden from assistive tech and the tone is color alone, so keep a sign, or say the direction in `description`.

props.name: changeColor
props.description: The change's color. Unset, it's the sign's: `success` up, `danger` down, and none at zero. Set it where up is bad news, such as a cost or an error rate.

props.name: description
props.description: A note under the figure ("since last month"), as a `Stat.Description` last.

props.name: size
props.description: The figure's size, a step of Bulma's size scale. The label, the change and the note stay small.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a `Skeleton` in place of `value`, one line of the figure tall, and sets `aria-busy` on the Stat. The label, the change and the note render as given. With a `Stat.Value` child, it only sets `aria-busy`: the child renders as given, so put a `Skeleton` in it yourself.

props.name: children
props.description: `Stat.Label`, `Stat.Value`, `Stat.Change` and `Stat.Description`, for anything the props don't cover, such as a unit or an info tip. They render between `label` and `value`. They're this Stat's own parts, so not another Stat: that would be a list inside this one's. The Stat finds a `Stat.Label` or `Stat.Value` among them by type, so one rendered from inside a component of your own isn't seen.

props.name: textColor
props.description: Text color helper. It colors the figure; the label, the change and the note keep their own colors. Inside `Stats`, a Stat without one takes the row's.

props.name: bgColor
props.description: Background color helper.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the root, a `<div>` inside `Stats` or a `<dl>` on its own.

parts.summary: A change written with its sign, such as "+12%", after an arrow that repeats the direction: a `<dd>`, green when it's up and red when it's down unless `color` says otherwise. The sign is in the text, written by `Intl` for the locale, so a screen reader hears the direction; the arrow is hidden from assistive tech, and the color repeats the direction for sighted readers rather than carry it.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes to apply.

props.name: value
props.description: The change, as Stat's `change`. One that rounds to zero in its format, such as `0.0004` at one decimal place of a percentage, reads as zero, so it gets no arrow and no color of its own.

props.name: format
props.description: As Stat's `changeFormat`: yours replace the default, and `signDisplay: 'exceptZero'` is added unless you set a `signDisplay`.

props.name: locale
props.description: As Stat's `locale`. Unset, the Stat's.

props.name: color
props.description: As Stat's `changeColor`. Unset, it's the sign's: `success` up, `danger` down, and none at zero. Set, it applies at zero too.
